title: Stability in Virtue and the Origin of Incest
english: It is written for every master of teaching to be carried forward: 'Stand fast therefore, and do not again be held by the yoke of slavery' (Gal 5:1). And the Psalmist says thankfully: 'You have set my feet upon a rock' (Ps 40:2). But concerning evils, as always rubbing against bad things, it has been said: 'The shaking of their feet shall not stand' (Ps 68:6). For it is a great sin to be always moving in evil, which the word says is not to be in Zion, wishing it: 'Set yourself, O Zion' (Ps 69:28).

This is what the blessed David, possessing this, sang so that he might not fall from it: 'And let not the hand of sinners shake me' (Ps 69:28), which is: the deeds of a sinner, of the devil, may not turn me away from virtue. And Cain knew his wife, and having conceived, she bore Enoch (Gen 4:17). And he was building a city, and he named the city after the name of his son Enoch.

Some seek from where Cain had a wife, since there were none other than Adam and Eve, from whom the evildoers introduce brother-marriage. It was necessary for them to realize that from this brother-marriage is not introduced. For if, while others existed, he used the relation to his sister, the word was probable; but if, of no one existing, it happened for the establishment of succession, where is there room for brother-marriage, such as being of another could be accepted for a yoke-mate? A word is also carried among the Stoics, seeking whether, if the conflagration of the world should happen and the one wise man of the human race should remain with his daughter to watch over the ember, knowing that the world will be decorated again, which is why there is a need for succession, if it is used properly for the daughter; and the word seems to them not unfamiliar regarding there not being another.

This also seems to have happened concerning the daughters of Lot, which the lovers blame, but none of the wise. For they do not suppose there was another man because of the having happened of the burning of those cities, but having also taken them as maidens, that all the land had undergone such things previously, they say: 'Behold, our father has grown old, and there is no man who shall come to us, as it is fitting for all the land; come, and let us give our father wine' (Gen 19:31). And that they did not do this through passion, but having left an ember, one came and turned the other to do this, which she would not have done quickly if she had served through passion, but by the same [means].

As the first managed, so also the second did, for the sake of fuller succession. Cain, then, is not to be blamed in these things, even if he erred in many. It must be noted that it did not say: “Cain knew his sister,” but “his wife”; for this is the proper designation of succession. One might ask how, with some five persons named — the parents of Cain and himself and his wife — he is said to build a city, a thing needing a multitude; and the questioner will also demand the reason why they made a city, when one cave or even a very small dwelling sufficed for habitation; to which […] — the rest of the page is blank.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The distinction between hearing and being instructed
english: Humans are animals of choice, participating in sciences; for they do not live by sensation alone like the irrational, but the virtue of the rational is already shown through being inventors of arts. The first point regarding the literal sense is this; the things regarding the ascent are these.

The cattle-tender is different from the shepherd; for the one grazes with science, but the cattle-tender does not. Abel was the righteous shepherd, governing his irrational powers—the desiring, the appetitive, and the spirited—according to the right reason; but the cattle-tender, lacking science and being a certain pleasure-seeker, is subject to the sensations alone, not ruling them but being ruled by them.

And as a clear example, it would be said in this way: The physician uses touch differently than one looking toward pleasure; this one, then, is a kind of cattle-tender, but the physician is a shepherd, for he uses reason with sensation. In the same way, regarding smell and the other sensations, the one using them with reason is best. For reasoning begins the sensation, and if the reasoning is held in check, the man receives the qualities according to the passions, such as being called a lion through the spirited part, a fox through the cunning, and a serpent through the earthly part, and also being called a horse through the pleasurable part; for they say, 'You have become like mares' (Psalm 55:19), and other men are called such because, being entirely of the sensations, they produce nothing divine, like us; for he says, 'Do not become like a horse and a similar creature, which have no understanding' (Psalm 49:20).

The cattle-tender is such, being a certain base person, not dwelling in a house but in tents, a precarious thing, not imitating those who dwell in tents for the sake of entering into the house, who also say as in the Psalm: 'How lovely are your dwellings, O Lord of hosts: my soul longs and even faints for the courts of the Lord' (Psalm 84:1-2); for the one progressing from tents desires the courts, singing: 'I will go in the way of a wonderful habitation until I reach the house of God' (Psalm 77:13). The other brother is 'he who showed the harp and the lyre' (Psalm 33:2), being his brother in righteousness; for he has neighbors for the enjoyment of pleasures and the deception through music being worked upon the ears; for 'woe' to 'those who rise up...'

Chasing the morning and the evening, remaining blind; for wine will intoxicate them; for they drink wine with lyres and psalteries, but they do not look upon the works of the Lord. And the other [one] crafts war-gear from bronze and iron, the bronze making its sound, just as Paul writes, 'I have become a sounding bronze' (1 Cor 13:1); and he himself is also a worker of iron, being a certain sophist and deceiving through seeming probabilities.

And Lamech said to his wives, Adam and Zillah: 'Hear my voice, women of Lamech; be instructed by my words; for I have killed a man for a wound, and a young man for a bruise' (Gen 4:23-24); for seventy times seven has been avenged from Cain, and from Lamech seventy times seven. I believe that being instructed is brought about only by divine instruction, and it differs from hearing, when it is joined with it; for the one, being instructed, is the hearing of that which is near, but the hearing is the hearing of that which is far off, and the word is not near. And in Isaiah, 'Hear, O heaven, and be instructed, O earth, for the Lord has spoken' (Isa 30:2), is not said in parallel, which is also 'Be instructed, O heaven, and I will speak' (Isa 40:9)—for instead of 'Pay attention,' other interpreters say 'Be instructed'—'and let the earth hear the words from my mouth' (Isa 30:2). And they say such an observation exists: when the law was being given by God, since it happened to be near the heavenly works, for this reason the heaven is commanded to be instructed; but when they departed from the upright citizenship, as to become far from the earth, then it is said, 'Hear, O heaven'—for they happened to be far—'and be instructed, O earth,' for this [earth] was near through its attachments. Therefore Lamech did not say 'Hear' and 'Be instructed' in parallel, but rather we have observed the difference between them in the Scripture not to be untimely; and what is it that we should learn, he says: 'Hear my voice, women of Lamech; be instructed by my words' (Gen 4:23). And someone might say that the voice and the words are in parallel; but he who seeks precision even regarding these would say that regarding the voice he ordered 'Hear,' but regarding the words he ordered the more precise thing, which is to be instructed.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Lineage and the Definition of Man
english: Observing the difference, someone might say that John was a 'voice crying out' (Matt 3:3), taking the immediate word of the scriptures to mean 'voice', but the mystical mind to mean 'logos'. 'That I killed a man unto my wound and a youth unto my blindness' (Gen 4:24). It is said in the book of the Testament by Lamech that Cain was killed accidentally; for he was turned back while building some wall, behind which Cain was, who was also killed accidentally. That he was killed, he says, 'unto my wound' happened, but that he did not do it willfully, 'unto my blindness' [happened].

Adam knew (Gen 4:1) Eve his wife, and having conceived, she bore a son and named his name Seth, saying: 'God has raised up for me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain killed' (Gen 4:25). Previously, regarding the things signified by 'knew' (Gen 4:1), we did not say that Adam's knowing Eve his wife meant standing beside her, but rather that they had come together, which also now signifies. She, 'having conceived she bore a son', whom 'and named Seth, saying: God has raised up for me seed instead of Abel, whom Cain killed' (Gen 4:25).

Those bringing forward different natures of the Valentinian heresy, saying that their unsuited virtue is that which they call earthly, and the unsuited evil, which they indeed also call spiritual, saying a third is the psychic, which is considered by them as being a mixture; and they take Cain as a sign of the unsuited virtue, and Abel of the spiritual, referring the remainder to Seth. It is not of the present time to refute this impious heresy, so that the word may not be defiled; but we also consider the word of Eve to be a testimony to the manner of Seth. For instead of the excellent Abel, this is interpreted as 'watering/refreshing'; and this is a symbol of life-giving provision; for this 'bringing forward' [one] must be interpreted as Abel having a brother, so that being first and more perfect, he might bring forward to God the spiritual sacrifices in the manner of a priest, while Seth brings forward a secondary struggle, through watering and teaching, those being instructed to God, who instead of Cain exists as someone self-willed and throwing [blame] upon himself; for [he is] a creature [interpreted as...].

Genesis 5:26. And to Seth there was born a son, and he named his name Enos; he hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God. The holy ones from the holy often possess both a physical descent from them and a descent according to the soul, in the same manner that Abraham became the father of Isaac, and Isaac of Jacob, and Jacob of Joseph; for these exist both by human succession from them and have become imitators of their virtue. But Esau became the son of Isaac according to the flesh alone, becoming a stranger to him through his own will; for he happened to be worthless. Seth, therefore, being placed instead of the righteous, begets Enos the righteous, who instead of the name of the Lord is called man; of such a nature, his soul's virtue declaring the 'according to the image' and the state of a truly existing man; for Enos is a 'man' among the Hebrews.

One must also add what is proper to man: 'He' says, 'hoped to call upon the name of the Lord'; and this is a virtuous practice for such a man. The hope that this truly is, is to become like God as much as possible; and to hope to call upon the name of the Lord God while simultaneously subjecting oneself to authority and to divine teaching is the hope.

Genesis 1:1–2. This is the book of the generations of men. On the day God made Adam, He made him according to the image of God; male and female He made them, and blessed them, and named their name Adam, on the day He made them. Here he called the narrative concerning Adam and his succession down to the present. Before the sixth day, on which man came into being, it was called the 'book of heaven and earth'; for we had finished that whole narrative concerning those before man, setting down another beginning of the generation of men. He calls 'generation' the word describing His making, just as it is said concerning Jesus: 'The book of the generation of Jesus Christ,' speaking according to the flesh; for the eternal [one] is unknown to men; for it is said: 'Who shall recount his lineage?' Just as we did not say the six days were a multitude of days, so also not the one...
